attributions.surface_quote: Guarding the Tao ensures a continuance of long life, with vigour and success.

canonical_statement: The attributes of the Tao (Tê) constitute the fundamental nature of reality, distinct from conventional moral virtue.

attributions.surface_quote: Tê is not virtue in our common meaning, but the attributes of the Tao.

canonical_statement: Effective governance and existence are achieved through non-purposive, quiet alignment with the Tao.

attributions.surface_quote: Occupying the throne according to the Tao, noiselessly and purposelessly.

canonical_statement: The Tao operates through a method of contraries to achieve outcomes.

attributions.surface_quote: aphorisms illustrating the procedure of the Tao “by contraries”

canonical_statement: The Taoist principle of 'doing nothing' is a purposeful method rather than absolute inaction.

attributions.surface_quote: Taoistic “doing nothing” was not an absolute quiescence and inaction, but had a method

canonical_statement: The sage achieves objectives by anticipating and forestalling difficulties.

attributions.surface_quote: sage accordingly accomplishes his objects easily by forestalling in his measures all difficulties

canonical_statement: The Tao exerts a powerful and beneficent influence on the world that transcends human contrivance.

attributions.surface_quote: powerful and beneficent influence of the Tao in government

canonical_statement: Humility and self-effacement are fundamental mechanisms for achieving influence and precedence.

attributions.surface_quote: places himself in his qualities below others, his person is above them

canonical_statement: The moral qualities of the Tao are inherent to the nature of the Tao itself.

attributions.surface_quote: the qualities, we may venture to say, of the Tao itself

canonical_statement: The Tao functions as the fundamental course of events and universal providence.

attributions.surface_quote: Heaven is equivalent to the Tao, the course of events—Providence.

canonical_statement: The Tao operates through the mechanism of contraries or opposites.

attributions.surface_quote: The procedure of the Tao by contraries, or opposites.

canonical_statement: The Tao acts as the singular, unifying principle that comprehends and governs all existence.

attributions.surface_quote: The Tao comprehends and rules all Laozi’s teachings.

canonical_statement: The indulgence of appetites and passions accelerates the cessation of physical existence.

attributions.surface_quote: indulgences of the appetites and passions... tend to shorten life

canonical_statement: The sage preserves life by avoiding the external demonstration of power and self-importance.

attributions.surface_quote: The sage loves himself... but without any demonstration that he is doing so.

canonical_statement: True self-love manifests as a commitment to the welfare of the collective rather than personal aggrandizement.

attributions.surface_quote: he reputes himself as one who must devote himself to the happiness of the people.

canonical_statement: The ultimate authority of a ruler is maintained through accessibility and benevolence rather than through the imposition of fear.

attributions.surface_quote: If the people do not fear the ruler's majesty, but approach him easily, majesty is maximized.

canonical_statement: The operations and judgments of Heaven are inscrutable to ordinary human understanding.

attributions.surface_quote: Who can know the mind of Heaven? Only the sage can do so.

canonical_statement: Heaven acts as the ultimate arbiter and executor of justice regarding human transgressions.

attributions.surface_quote: It is Heaven, which... takes note of the transgressions of men.

canonical_statement: The fundamental nature of the Tao is characterized by weakness and humility rather than force.

attributions.surface_quote: To trust in one’s force is contrary to the Tao, whose strength is more in weakness.

canonical_statement: The Way of Heaven is inherently unselfish and magnanimous, contrasting with the selfish nature of human action.

attributions.surface_quote: The Way of Heaven contrasts with the way of man, selfish and contracted.

canonical_statement: Water serves as an emblematic representation of the Tao's properties.

attributions.surface_quote: Water was Laozi’s favourite emblem of the Tao.

canonical_statement: Action aligned with the Tao produces results that appear paradoxical or unlikely.

attributions.surface_quote: The most unlikely results follow from action according to the Tao.

canonical_statement: The Tao functions as the ultimate arbiter of justice and natural order in the universe.

attributions.surface_quote: Par. 3 decides the question by the action of heaven, which is the Tao.

canonical_statement: Alignment with the Tao yields superior long-term outcomes compared to the pursuit of individual self-interest.

attributions.surface_quote: He who holds fast to the Tao will be better off in the end.

canonical_statement: The Tao operates through the mechanism of contraries, which is only intelligible to those who have mastered its nature.

attributions.surface_quote: The Tao proceeds, and by contraries in a way that only the master can understand.

canonical_statement: The fundamental nature of the Tao is characterized by a paradoxical abundance achieved through non-hoarding.

attributions.surface_quote: He hoards not, and thereby his affluence displays.

canonical_statement: The Taoist principle of action is inherently beneficial and non-injurious to all beings.

attributions.surface_quote: Heaven's Tao benefits and does not injure.
